kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source facts.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the two species rows, the two ionization strips, the TCA margin note, the pKa row, and the ionized-species graph; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The two-axis reading (the equilibrium axis: 'Ionized species are trapped in urine and cleared quickly. Neutral forms can be reabsorbed.' — the weak-acid strip RCOOH (lipid soluble) ⇌ RCOO– + H+ (trapped) trapped by ALKALINE urine, the weak-base strip RNH3+ (trapped) ⇌ RNH2 + H+ (lipid soluble) trapped by ACIDIC urine; and the treatment axis: alkalinize the urine with sodium bicarbonate for weak-acid overdoses [phenobarbital, methotrexate, aspirin/salicylates], acidify the urine with ammonium chloride for severe alkalosis with weak bases [TCAs, amphetamines], with the TCA caveat — bicarbonate initially treats the sodium-channel-blocking CARDIAC toxicity and does NOT accelerate drug elimination — plus the pKa graph reading: 50% ionized at pH = pKa, weak acids ionize as pH rises above pKa, weak bases ionize as pH falls below pKa, 'pKa = more acidic' / 'pKa = more basic') — KYP's synthesis of the page into one reading protocol.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the rows, strips, note, and graph sequentially without a unified protocol; the two-axis framing is KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP mnemonics (1 — ACID-in-ALKALI / BASE-in-ACID: the direction rule; 2 — PMA gets the BICARB: Phenobarbital · Methotrexate · Aspirin, the weak-acid overdose set, with sodium bicarbonate; 3 — AA ACIDifies: Amphetamines And TCAs, the weak-base set, trapped in acidic environments, ammonium chloride for severe alkalosis; 4 — 50/50 AT pKa: the pKa rule with the graph reading). The page prints NO mnemonic in this section — all four codes are KYP-original designs.
kypExtensions.rationale: Book 231's Urine pH and drug elimination section prints NO margin mnemonic (unlike the PEA mnemonic on book 230); all four codes are KYP-original designs.

notes: Census (pdfimages + VLM): NO raster images on the page (pdfimages -list returned zero rows for pdf 253). The Urine pH and drug elimination section has ONE vector graph (the Ionized species formation (%) vs pH plot with the Weak acid and Weak base curves, 100/50/0 gridlines, 4/8/12/14 pH x-axis, 'pKa: 9.2', 'pKa = more acidic', 'pKa = more basic') — redrawn as an ORIGINAL_KYP_REDRAW vector graphic in the registry visual (no photographs, no copyrighted artwork reproduced). The two ionization reaction strips (RCOOH (lipid soluble) ⇌ RCOO– + H+ (trapped); RNH3+ (trapped) ⇌ RNH2 + H+ (lipid soluble)) print in the text layer as short chemical species phrases and are carried verbatim in the note's table blocks and the visual's species panels (ORIGINAL_KYP_ADAPTATION) — short attributed phrases, not artwork reproductions. The page prints NO margin mnemonic for this section; the KYP memory layer adds four original codes (ACID-in-ALKALI/BASE-in-ACID, PMA gets the BICARB, AA ACIDifies, 50/50 AT pKa). No copyrighted photographs exist on the page; nothing reproduced. NOTE: page 253 (book 231) ALSO contains the Dosage calculations section (Loading dose = Cp × Vd / F; Maintenance dose = Cp × CL × τ / F), which is covered by the separate pending dosage-calculations topic and is NOT covered by this topic's evidence or visual. NO Drug Metabolism (PH3) or Elimination kinetics (PH4) content appears on this page — those live on pdf 252 (book 230) and are already produced.
